step_1_baseline_gate.note: Baseline rule gate only checked wildcards (*). PassRole + Lambda was unencoded, resulting in a silent pass (0 violations).

step_2_gemma_audit.threat_explanation: This policy grants broad permissions to create and invoke Lambda functions and allows the IAM role to be passed to any service. This poses a significant risk as it allows attackers to potentially gain control of AWS resources by passing arbitrary roles to newly created Lambda functions.
combination_risks: IAM:PassRole combined with lambda:CreateFunction allows privilege escalation via role assumption.

step_3_discovery_loop_codification.codified_rego_rule: deny contains msg if { some s1 in get_statements; s1.Effect == 'Allow'; has_action(s1, 'iam:PassRole'); some s2 in get_statements; s2.Effect == 'Allow'; has_action(s2, 'lambda:CreateFunction'); msg := '[Rule: passrole_lambda_escalation] PassRole paired with lambda:CreateFunction allows privilege escalation.' }

violations.message: [Rule: passrole_lambda_escalation] PassRole paired with lambda:CreateFunction allows privilege escalation via role assumption.

step_3_discovery_loop_codification.note: Breaks the circular check: before codifying, Conftest was 0 violations. Once codified, Conftest flags the un-remediated policy (1 violation) and mathematically verifies the remediated policy drops to 0 violations.
